title: Minimal-evidence security onramp experiment for enterprise contract velocity
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Objective: run a controlled experiment that reduces up-front evidence burden for a subset of enterprise prospects by providing a curated 'minimal evidence' attestation pack and a pricing/onboarding trigger. The hypothesis is that a lightweight attestation option will increase contract velocity and win-rate for mid-market deals without materially increasing legal or security review overhead.

Scope: create a 5-document minimal pack (architecture diagram, encryption summary, data flow, retention policy excerpt, CAIQ condensed answers) and a clear product pricing/onboarding rule that maps eligible deals to the onramp. Eligibility criteria will be based on deal size (<= $250k ARR) and non-regulated industry verticals. The experiment will run for 8 weeks and target inbound sales-qualified opportunities routed to the self-serve + sales-assisted funnel.

Experiment design: A/B test at opportunity level: Control = standard full attestation workflow; Variant = minimal-evidence pack + one-click attestation acceptance and optional follow-up checklist. Instrumentation will track funnel conversion, time to countersignature, number of security escalations, legal review hours, and post-sale support tickets related to compliance.

Why unique: Instead of bundling broader pricing credits, this experiment ties a lightweight evidence flow to a product onramp that reduces friction early in negotiations. We avoid duplicating prior SIQ/attestation bundle efforts by focusing on strategy (eligibility and trigger) rather than catalog breadth.

Outcomes we will evaluate: increased close rate within 60 days, decrease in average days to signature, minimal increase in security/legal touchpoints, and revenue retention after 6 months.

Rollout plan: 1) Draft condensed CAIQ extract and minimal pack (Confluence draft); 2) Legal + Security sign-off on pack and liability language; 3) Update pricing-led contract templates with an onramp clause; 4) Instrument CRM (HubSpot) flags and Looker dashboard; 5) Pilot with 10 active opportunities; 6) Measure and iterate.

Risks & mitigations: If Security flags increase, pause pilot and revert to full workflow; include automatic follow-up audit to collect full evidence post-signature for any red-flag customers; log every exception for analysis.

Links and artifacts: Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENT/Minimal+Evidence+Onramp (draft); Google Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1OnrampDraft; GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/attest-onramp/pull/12; Dashboard (Looker): https://looker.redwood.ai/dashboards/attest_onramp_pilot
acceptance_criteria: Legal and Security sign-off obtained for the five-document minimal pack
CRM flagging implemented and pilot cohort defined in HubSpot
Instrumentation capturing funnel conversion and review escalations
Pilot executed on at least 10 live opportunities with A/B segmentation
Decision criteria and playbook documented for scale/rollback
